text:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT 8221 created: inference-runtime high 95p latency + 5xx spike. Paging @oncall-1 (samira). Autocreated from alert: continuous-batching.latency > 200ms for 5m.

samira: On it. I'm seeing a huge jump in KV cache misses in the model shards dashboard, miss rate ~78% vs baseline 2%. Noted spike at 14:21 UTC around deploy.

michael: I rolled a small change earlier to how function/tool-calls are encoded in structured output (adds a `tool_metadata` header) — could be changing tokenization boundaries and breaking batching grouping heuristics.

jess: That matches — function-calling responses now include a long JSON block in a single token group which prevents prefix-sharing, so continuous batching isn't finding prefix alignment, causing each request to be its own batch => KV cache localities blow up.

oncall-2: Paging in. What's the immediate customer impact?

customer-success: We received 3 tickets from enterprise customers (chat streams). Errors 502/504 starting 14:20, about ~10-15% of requests failing, some severe tail latency for others.

samira: Confirmed: error trace shows `batch_assembly_timeout` and `kv_lookup_timeout` for affected shards. Latency SLO violated for a subset of routes. We'll need a hotfix to batching config and short-term KV eviction to let caches rebuild with new grouping.

michael: Proposed quick mitigations: (1) temporarily disable the new structured tool metadata grouping so batching heuristics treat output as normal tokens; (2) reduce continuous batching max_window_ms to favor smaller, more deterministic batches; (3) force-evict stale KV cache shards to avoid polluted entries.

jess: I can revert the grouping in the runtime with a feature-flag. Hotfix command (will require admin token):

```
# disable tool metadata grouping
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/feature-flag
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
  -d '{"flag":"runtime.tool_metadata_grouping","value":false}'
```

samira: I'll apply the batching config change first since it's lower risk. Patch via admin API:

```
# lower continuous batching window
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/runtime/config
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
  -d '{"continuous_batching.max_window_ms":30,"continuous_batching.min_batch_size":2}'
```

infra-bot: config-update: continuous_batching.max_window_ms -> 30 applied by samira at 2024-06-12T14:33:05Z.

samira: Pushed the config. Observability: batch sizes dropped from avg 24 -> avg 3, 95p latency dropped from 420ms -> 120ms within 90s. KV miss rate improving but still high for a few shards.

michael: Okay I'll flip the feature-flag revert for tool metadata grouping while we investigate long-term fix. Rolling revert to canary first (pool-a).

infra-bot: feature-flag update: runtime.tool_metadata_grouping=false rolled to canary pool-a at 2024-06-12T14:36:40Z.

oncall-2: After canary looks good, promote globally. Michael, can you also queue a targeted KV eviction for model-x shards that showed blowups? Command below:

```
# evict KV cache for shard ranges 12-15 for model-x
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/kv/evict
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
  -d '{"model":"model-x","shard_range":[12,15]}'
```

infra-bot: kv-evict job 984 queued by michael. Started at 2024-06-12T14:40:12Z.

samira: After eviction and feature-flag rollback, error rate dropped to baseline and 95p latency stable ~110ms. Customers reporting reduced errors.

lucas: Confirmed CS updated customers with a short blurb and ETA for postmortem. No data exfil detected.

jess: Root cause summary for postmortem: structured function/tool outputs created large tokenized blocks that prevented prefix alignment used by continuous batching heuristics, resulting in many single-request batches and massive KV cache miss amplification.

michael: Follow-ups: (1) add unit + load tests that simulate long structured outputs + function-calling to catch batching regressions; (2) defensive limit on token-block length that will bypass tool-metadata grouping for high-variance responses; (3) improve metrics to detect batch-locality degradation faster (heatmap).

oncall-2: Taking the incident for next 3 hours. Handing off context: hotfix applied, feature-flag reverted globally at 14:42Z, KV eviction completed by 14:46Z, customer-impact window ~14:20-14:34Z. Samira handing over notes in incident channel.

samira: Handoff done. If anything spikes again ping me. I'll start the postmortem doc and link it once ready.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 8221 status -> mitigated. P1 -> P2. Please file postmortem at /incidents/8221 and assign owners.

customer-success: Customers updated, major accounts asked for timeline; will wait for postmortem and offer credits if needed.

jess: Quick action item for eng-ml: review the structured-output serializer to minimize accidental huge contiguous token groups.

michael: noted. I'll also add a canary that injects `tool_metadata` shapes into continuous-batching sim harness.

oncall-2: Closing thread for live mitigation. Will keep monitoring for 2 hours.

samira: Thanks team. Great triage. :thumbsup:
